stem: Why is one unusually high production cycle insufficient to prove a sustained improvement?
choices: One unusually high cycle proves improvement if it exceeds the historical average by enough to be operationally meaningful.
Context should be excluded from KPI interpretation because it makes the metric less objective.
The newest cycle should receive the greatest weight because it reflects current production capability.
Sustained improvement requires repeated comparable observations and context for changes in population, process, timing, or denominator that could explain the one-cycle spike.
rationale: A single high result may reflect real improvement, random variation, a changed population, a denominator shift, unusual conditions, or another one-time factor. A sustained trend requires multiple comparable observations and enough context to know the metric still means the same thing over time. Recency alone cannot establish durability.
